title: Close out the governance residuals carried by the 2026-09-22 remediation rounds
goal: Clear the residual gaps the 2026-09-22 rounds left behind and could not close inside their own scope: two committed credentials, a Redis test helper that let a required CI gate go green while skipping, a boundary baseline whose stale entries could silently whitelist a reintroduced import, a dead unwired architecture checker, a task-packet checker that reported 166 errors on history, and a generator that produced modules the check:generated gate could not identify. Record pantheon-ops synchronization as an explicit deferral with its real blocker.
statusNote: 2026-09-23: each residual fixed at its source with a ratchet where the class can recur (Redis env contract, stale-baseline failure, legacy-allowlist staleness, marker consistency). pantheon-ops sync stays deferred: the ops working tree carries 269 uncommitted files from another session and .foundation/foundation-release.lock.json already records baseline-swap as blocked on exactly that, so swapping over it would mix lineage.
technicalDebtNote: Three gaps remain real and are untouched here: the low-code generator still does not write the marker into the 11 stable artifacts it rewrites (only into the module files it generates), so check:generated covers those 11 by name rather than by marker; 17 pre-template task docs stay in config/task-packet-legacy-docs.json until someone migrates or deletes them; and pantheon-ops is 31+ commits behind the v0.12.1 lock it consumes.
dependencyLayers: platform governance tooling (harness checkers, CI workflow env)

blocks: pantheon-ops foundation sync (needs the next foundation release cut from this state)

in: remove the committed Redis and MySQL dev credentials from docs/README.md, two evidence transcripts and the QA-setup script fallback list
make pkg/testredis accept the runtime env var names and add PANTHEON_TEST_REDIS_REQUIRED so a misconfigured job fails instead of skipping
point the quality.yml backend-tests job at the test Redis variable and set the required flag in both Go test jobs
delete the three stale auth -> system/iam/user entries from config/boundary-baseline.json and make stale entries fail check-boundaries --strict
delete scripts/check-arch-boundaries.mjs and port its only live invariant into check-boundaries.mjs
give check-task-packet.mjs a legacy allowlist with staleness detection and wire it into the docs-governance job
mark every file the low-code generator exports and guard the marker sentence against the gate
close the 2026-07-20 review verdict that contradicted its completed manifest
out: any change to runtime behaviour, API, permissions, menus, i18n, database or seed
pantheon-ops baseline swap (deferred with a recorded blocker)
the flaky full-smoke generator suite and the .golangci.yml v2 key drift

doNotTouch: admin SQL, seeds, permission matrix and i18n resources

commands: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l .
runtimeEvidence: testredis fail-loudly proof: PANTHEON_TEST_REDIS_REQUIRED=1 with no address fails the test instead of skipping
testredis var-name proof: with only PANTHEON_REDIS_ADDR set and a closed port the test now runs and reports the address source, where it previously skipped
check-boundaries negative proof: a probe import system/iam -> system/org/dept is reported as a finding
check-boundaries stale-baseline negative proof: a stale entry makes --strict exit 1 while report-only stays 0
check-task-packet negative proof: a stale legacy allowlist entry exits 1

evidenceRequired: credential sweep showing no committed dev credential remains
testredis before/after behaviour for the runtime env var name and the required flag
boundary gate output after the stale entries were removed, plus the two negative probes
task-packet checker output for default, --include-legacy and a stale allowlist
generator marker test output and the check:generated run
review disposition incl. the ops-sync deferral
humanGates: none required (no permission, API, retention, menu or data surface changed) — PR gates plus non-author review
